title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：principle　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 principle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the clerk ① held the principle that no applicant in the office would have counted, and he said the holding was the whole of the month. The ② principle, meaning the rule itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a principle, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ principle in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ principle at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A principle, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the clerk said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the principle was the whole of the matter, meaning the belief and not the rule. The ⑥ principle, meaning the belief and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; principle, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a rule and a belief. He said the belief is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ principle had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ principle of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of counting; principle, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ principle I remember is the rule counted in the file, which closed in 1967 and is still counted as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ principle, my mother said in 1969, is the only rule that improves by being counted; every principle, she said, is a belief that has agreed to look like a rule. She said the belief was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 原则；原理（指办事处里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 原则；原理（指那条原则本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold the principle 坚持这一条原则
D. n. 原则；原理（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 原则之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的原则之事）
F. n. 原则；原理（指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一条）
G. n. 原则、信条（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 信条（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: hold the principle 意为“坚持这一条原则”，1960 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯清点的一条原则做了一遍。
principle 意为“原则；原理”，指那条原则本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
principle 意为“原则；原理”，指办事处里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
principle 意为“原则；原理”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
principle 意为“原则、信条”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条信条就是那件事的全部。
principle 意为“信条”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条原则，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
principle 意为“原则；原理”，指卷宗里写到、被清点的那一条，到 1965 年这一条成了卷宗里的一行。
principle 意为“原则之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的原则之事是一处办事处和三个月份的清点。
principle 意为“原则；原理”，我记得的是卷宗里清点过的那一条，1967 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一条。
principle 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，原则是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的原则。
